claims.statement: WebDecoy rules receive normalized request data and optional enrichment, agent, edge, caller-key, and prepared values; rules evaluate synchronously but can implement an asynchronous `prepare()` hook that stores network-derived values for later evaluation.

`RuleEngine` evaluates configured rules in order and continues through all of them; the first non-dry-run `DENY` or `THROTTLE` decides the final engine action, while per-rule outcomes and non-allow violations are retained.

Rule outcomes distinguish `RUN`, `DRY_RUN`, `NOT_RUN`, and `CACHED`; a dry-run match records a deny conclusion while retaining an `ALLOW` action, and a missing prerequisite can be surfaced as `NOT_RUN` rather than a normal passing evaluation.

Tripwire violations alone may forward the `wd_clearance` cookie token as `clearance`, so a backend can bind a deception hit to the actor fingerprint without attaching that token to other rule classes.

With an API client and rules present, the SDK buffers rule violations; the reporter flushes on a timer or buffer threshold, sends at most 100 events per request, drops failed batches, and flushes remaining events during destruction.
The SDK installs a default `tripwire()` when `rules` is omitted, while `rules: []` disables the rule engine; local rules remain usable without an API client.

Filters parse their expression at construction and explicitly return `NOT_RUN` when an expression references `ip.*` but IP enrichment is unavailable; locally populated bot and edge context are part of the rule context independently of enrichment.

A rate-limit rule chooses its bucket key from rule-specific `keyBy`, then the SDK caller key, then IP; it supports fixed or sliding windows, defaults to `THROTTLE`, and turns an async store not prepared before evaluation into an explicit `NOT_RUN` result.

The default `MemoryRateLimitStore` is a synchronous, process-local in-memory store, so it is suitable for a single process but does not share counters across replicas or cold starts; a store interface separates inline synchronous consumption from asynchronously prepared consumption.

`UpstashRateLimitStore` is an asynchronous shared counter store implemented with HTTP `fetch` to Upstash Redis pipelines; it supports fixed and sliding algorithms, uses a timeout, and has explicit `onError` fail-open default or fail-closed behavior.
`TripwireRule` matches normalized paths against exact paths, prefixes, regular expressions, and enabled built-in scanner bait; it defaults to denial and produces 100-confidence metadata for a hit.
`honeytoken()` creates a random or configured trap path and a hidden nofollow, accessibility-hidden link, but callers must register that path with a tripwire and inject the link themselves.

`siteHoneytoken()` derives a stable HMAC path from a shared secret so replicas agree without stored coordination; optional rotation advertises today while keeping yesterday armed, and the injected link is designed to avoid cooperative-crawler and assistive-technology access.
Adapter-core derives and arms a site honeytoken before advertising it by adding a tripwire for every active path; on derivation failure it reports through an optional callback and returns no token.
Honeytoken link injection only rewrites complete `text/html` documents, inserts before `</body>` or `</html>`, avoids duplicate insertion, and leaves fragments or other content types unchanged.

`BotRule` enforces categories, named agents, or all AI agents identified from the User-Agent registry, with allow-list exemptions taking precedence; unrecognized user agents are allowed and a match is deliberately reported with confidence 70 rather than tripwire certainty.

`BotPolicy` resolves one registry-derived denied set and uses it both for its enforcing `BotRule` and generated `robots.txt`; it identifies denied agents that do not document robots compliance, because robots instructions are voluntary rather than enforcement.

`attackSignatures()` is intentionally a small curated signature rule rather than a WAF: it defaults to path and query inspection, makes body and header inspection opt-in, excludes cookies even when headers are scanned, and should use dry run for higher-false-positive surfaces.

Attack-signature matching bounds attacker-controlled work by truncating each inspected part and decoding percent encoding at most twice; matches expose signature/location metadata and configuration supports exclusions, throttling, and dry run.

`protect()` builds one context, performs prerequisite fetches and preparation when required, evaluates local rules before cache or remote detection, and does not cache local refusals so rate limits advance and tripwire hits remain reportable on every request.
